version.changelog: Capabilities & Data Flow declarations + CLI hardening (SkillSpector audit response, #91)

llm.summary: This skill coherently wraps a disclosed ZooData web-extraction API, with credential and credit-use caveats users should understand.

dimensions.detail: The skill sends requested URLs, search queries, crawl options, and the API key to api.zoodata.ai; that is disclosed and proportionate to the web-extraction purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package installation is required; the Python wrapper is stdlib-only and requires a ZooData API key supplied by environment variable or optional config file.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Some trigger phrases are broad, but the runtime instructions stay within user-requested web extraction and call for confirmation before costly large crawls or deep-scrapes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no privilege escalation or autonomous local persistence, but the docs offer an optional plaintext credential file under the user's home directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is structured scraping, search, mapping, and crawling, and the bundled CLI only exposes matching ZooData WebTools endpoints.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending requested URLs, queries, and crawl parameters to ZooData and spending API credits. Prefer ZOODATA_API_KEY in your environment or a protected config file, and confirm large crawls before running them.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger examples map to the advertised scrape/search/map/crawl behavior; the artifact also discloses credit costs and says to confirm before large crawls or deep-scrapes.
[SQP-2] expected: The bearer-token example is a placeholder-style value used to document required authentication, not evidence of a real embedded secret; clearer placeholder wording would reduce confusion.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Inspection found the documented token value is hms_live_xxx, which appears illustrative rather than a usable credential, so this does not support a malicious or Review verdict.
[RA2] expected: Optional plaintext API-key persistence is disclosed and common for CLI tools, but users should prefer environment variables or protect the config file permissions.
